name: Adoption effort
purpose: Steps and files needed for a newcomer, following only the standard, to add a passing solution or a passing new repository. It cannot yet separate the two ways of applying ESOI, from the documents only or with the tools, because no trial of either is recorded.
record: The steps and files a newcomer needs, following only the standard, to add a passing solution or a passing new repository, noted per trial.

name: Intents whose solutions one paragraph and one diagram explain as the code builds them
purpose: Every intent's solutions are explained by one coherent paragraph and one diagram that match how they relate in the records and in the code, in a hierarchy a reader can take in.
record: Per intent, from `python3 -m esoi.structure.structure_check.coherence --json`: whether solution_coherence names every solution and states every uses edge in one sentence, the roots and the solutions no edge reaches, whether solution_diagram draws exactly the uses edges with what each passes, the share of uses edges with both ends in code that the code shows, the share of import edges between the intent's solutions that a uses path covers, the largest fan-out and the depth.
disadvantages: Reads the selected implementation's uses only; the code evidence is an import, a named id or interface, or an Assembler over declared seats, not a proof that one part calls the other; whether the paragraph reads as one line of thought is left to a later model-judged stage, run only when a reader finds a passing paragraph unclear.

name: Metric record kept
purpose: Measures whether a piece of work records its metric before and after, as rows in the results log pinned to the commit, so the change can be judged later.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for the live record implementation, one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash.
disadvantages: It sees that the rows exist and carry the slice, not whether the metric chosen for the work was the right one.

name: Ranking correctness
purpose: Share of pinned result sets where the leaderboard's verdict matches the known right verdict, including ties and different case sets.
record: The share of pinned result sets where the leaderboard's verdict matches the known right verdict, per run of the ranking cases.

name: Provenance completeness
purpose: Share of latest results with a clean commit, a case hash, cost and tokens, run through shipped code.
record: The share of latest results with a clean commit, a case hash, cost and tokens, per run of the provenance cases.

name: Promotion correctness
purpose: Measures whether a clear winner is promoted only on current, comparable, verified results and only where the policy allows it.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for each implementation on the same cases, one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash.

name: Decisions backed by current results
purpose: Measures the share of selection decisions that cited a current result, and the spend per decision.
record: Per run of the staleness cases: cases passed out of cases run (a stale or missing result is reported and a current one is not), one row per run in the results log; per decision: whether the cited result was current when chosen and what the runs behind it cost, noted in the decision's record.

name: Assembly by name cases
purpose: Measures whether the assembler builds parts by validated name as its solution defines, and refuses what it must refuse.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for the live assembler, one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash.
disadvantages: It sees the risks its cases name (hostile names, cycles, unmet needs, concurrent assembles, the examples in the docs), not how a consumer's own assembly behaves.

name: Consumer soundness
purpose: Unmapped integration points, consumer stores not scored by the library's cases, and commits of pin lag.
record: The unmapped integration points, the consumer stores not scored by the library's cases, and the commits of pin lag, per consumer check.

name: Resolution correctness
purpose: Share of selection cases (name, override, default, typo, every listed implementation) that resolve as specified. No run measures the solution itself; its chosen implementation is measured through runtime-selection in the esoi-runtime intent.
record: The share of selection cases that resolve as specified, per run of the selection cases.

name: Navigable records
purpose: Measures whether a solution's specification and its code can be found from each other: in the same folder or one link apart, reachable from the top README, linked in one hop to the files or registry that implement it, kept once, and described by a README wherever an implementation lives.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for each layout on the same cases (one case per solution of this repository and of the adopting repositories measured), one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash. A case passes when the folder holding the solution's row and the folder of each implementation's code are the same folder or one link apart, the page of the folder holding its row, naming it, is within three clicks of the top README, the page that names it links in one hop to each file that holds its implementations (a code file, or the reference or registry file an implementation names), none of its records is kept in two places, every folder that holds the code of one of its implementations has a README.md, and laying the records out again writes the same pages.
disadvantages: The first stage cannot say whether a person finds the spec faster; it checks properties a navigable layout has. The adopting repositories are read from ESOI_GLANCE_ADOPTERS, so a machine without them runs only this repository's cases.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=each check this metric runs is rated 0 to 4 for a proposed layout before it is built; 0 means the layout would fail it on every folder; 2 means it would pass on about half of the folders; 4 means it would pass on every folder; the ratings are averaged with equal weights fixed before any layout is rated] > offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=competitive | when=the layout the checks pass on more solutions is the selected one] > human [sample=sample:3 | real=yes | gate=competitive | when=a person has looked for the spec of three solutions from their code in each layout and named the layout they would rather work in]
command: esoi run navigable_records --impl beside_code; esoi run navigable_records --impl esoi_folder

name: Record completeness
purpose: Share of records with every template field filled and every link resolving both ways.
record: The share of records with every template field filled and linked both ways, counted by the records cases and noted per review.

name: Adoption clarity
purpose: Whether a reader can tell, for each solution of an adopting repository, if it is adopted, specialized or its own, and whether no adopted solution restates its library.
record: Cases passed out of cases run on small fixture repositories: one per kind of record and one per finding of rule S53.
disadvantages: Fixtures cover the cases foreseen, not an application's real judgment of what is the same job.

name: Trace completeness
purpose: Share of files that reach a problem and an ideal through a component and a solution.
record: The share of files that reach a problem and an ideal, counted by the ownership cases and noted per review.

name: Structure cost against catches
purpose: Time and files the structure adds per change, against real violations it caught. No run measures it yet; the written weighing rule is applied by people.
record: The time and files the structure adds per change, against the real violations it caught, noted per period.

name: Violation detection
purpose: Share of injected violations reported by the right rule and path. It does not show the mistake behind each rule or what each rule has caught since.
record: The share of injected violations reported by the right rule and path, per run of the mutation cases.

name: Check dependability
purpose: Whether a clean tree is never flagged, an exception that no longer applies is reported, and how long the check takes.
record: Per run of the mutation cases: whether a clean tree is flagged, whether an unused exception is reported, and the check's run time.

name: Structure quality agreement
purpose: Whether the scorer agrees with labelled structural incidents and clean exemplars, and cannot be won by cutting files small: each case is a small project of a generic incident shape, and a comparison case needs the balanced real structure to score above the same project cut into tiny files.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for each arm on the same cases, balanced with cost and time (`[balance.score_structure_quality]`: accuracy 0.7, cost 0.15, time 0.15, fixed before any arm was scored), one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash. The number a scorer reports for a project has seven dimension weights fixed in balance.py: scope 0.20, coupling 0.20, size 0.15, reuse 0.15, behavior 0.15, flow 0.10, surface 0.05. Case sources, mixed in proportion: clean exemplars, incident shapes (a folder grown to a thousand files, a record list with very long functions, a merge that stripped interfaces, a library that names its consumer, one calculation copied six times, a cycle, no contract test, an unused surface), history (co-change with and without an import, and this library's own restructure from its git history), the foundation question (a shared kernel against a widely imported module that reaches into a solution), and the Goodhart moves (the project cut into tiny files, arms that stub a fat interface, a fat interface callers barely use, a reach-in behind a star re-export, a unit re-exporting its inside, one solution split into a chain of pass-throughs, a unit's own code moved into a foundation module).
disadvantages: The cases are fixtures of shapes foreseen, so they show the scorer sees each shape and not how often real code has it; the weights come from which failures cost most, not from fitted data; calls per request, the run-time symptom of duplicated work, needs traces and is a case source for a consumer, not read here; a static score cannot see behavior that was deleted, only running the contract tests can. The expert stage is specified at about 6000 tokens in and 600 out per project reviewed and has not been run.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=each incident shape and clean exemplar this metric holds is rated 0 to 4 for a proposed scorer before it is built; 0 means the scorer would misjudge it or could be won by cutting files small; 2 means it would judge about half of its variants right; 4 means it would judge every variant right; the ratings are averaged with equal weights fixed before any scorer is rated] > static [sample=full | real=no | gate=competitive | when=the cases are small projects built in the evaluation folder] > history [sample=full | real=no | gate=competitive | when=a repository has history to read] > expert [sample=full | real=yes | when=Joshua approved the spend, in stages of 3, 10 and 30 reviews]
command: esoi run score_structure_quality --impl balanced_static; esoi run score_structure_quality --impl file_size_only; esoi run score_structure_quality --impl expert_review

name: Behaviour adherence
purpose: Share of cases where an agent's reply acts by the principle the case tests, per principle, for each way of giving the agent the principles and for an agent without them.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for each arm on the same cases and sample, per principle, with restraint and kept-qualifier cases counted apart; one row per run in the results log, pinned to the commit, the case hash and the model.
disadvantages: The cases are written by the skill's author, so they test the behaviour the author anticipated; a reply graded by the model judge is only as good as the judge's agreement with people.

name: Local index lookup cases
purpose: Measures whether a lookup finds the project, its first file and its relations for a world of projects the guidance never named.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for each implementation on the same cases, one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash.
command: esoi run index_projects --impl live_index; esoi run index_projects --impl skill_rows; esoi run index_projects --impl records_only

name: README glanceability
purpose: Measures whether an intent folder's README tells a person on the first screen what the intent is, how its solutions fit and where to go next.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for each layout on the same cases (one case per intent folder of this repository and of the adopting repositories measured), one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash. A case passes when the vision statement, the solution coherence and the diagram end inside the first screen budget, every solution row has its entry call and selected implementation, every link resolves and the page links the sub-intents, the parent and the repository README, the text is finished (no em dash, placeholder marker or machine path), the page is identical when generated again from a fresh read, and the summary above the divider stays within its size budget.
disadvantages: The first stage cannot say whether a person finds the page clearer; it checks properties a clear page has. The adopting repositories are read from ESOI_GLANCE_ADOPTERS, so a machine without them runs only this repository's cases.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=each check this metric runs is rated 0 to 4 for a proposed page layout before it is built; 0 means the first screen would fail it on every folder; 2 means it would pass on about half of the folders; 4 means it would pass on every folder; the ratings are averaged with equal weights fixed before any layout is rated] > offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=competitive | when=the checks pass the selected layout on every folder and fail the page-less baseline] > human [sample=sample:3 | real=yes | gate=competitive | when=a person has opened three intent folders in each layout, side by side, and named the layout they would rather open first]
command: esoi run readme_at_a_glance --impl at_a_glance; esoi run readme_at_a_glance --impl full_page; esoi run readme_at_a_glance --impl links_page

name: README fidelity
purpose: Measures whether the generated page equals what the records say and is reported when it does not.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for each implementation on the same cases, one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash.

name: Review coverage
purpose: Share of records and verdicts present in the sheet, and share of reviewer edits that survive a rebuild and reach the repository.
record: The share of records and verdicts present in the sheet, and the share of reviewer edits that survive a rebuild and reach the repository, per sync.

name: Spec search correctness
purpose: Measures whether the records and items a request concerns are among the ranked keys for labelled requests (plain words, an item of another source, and a request about nothing) on the live records of this repository.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for each implementation on the same cases, one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash.
disadvantages: No vector search or judge is injected, because a stand-in would measure the stand-in, so the selected arm and the baseline tie here. What the vector search, the judge and the gate thresholds add is measured by the adopter that supplies them.
command: esoi run spec_search --impl gated; esoi run spec_search --impl lexical_only

name: Specification recall at k
purpose: Measures whether the records a request concerns are among the first few returned for labelled requests (direct, longer and noisier, naming two records, and concerning nothing), run on the live index of this repository's own records, and what share of the records' size the tier-0 scan costs. Nothing is simulated: the index and both ranking functions are the shipped code; a request whose words share nothing with its record is expected to be missed here and is the job of a consumer's vector search.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for each implementation on the same cases (a case passes when every expected record is in the top k, or the scan stays under its size ceiling), one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash.
command: esoi run spec_index --impl weighted_tfidf; esoi run spec_index --impl term_overlap

name: Newcomer effort
purpose: Measures how many steps and files a newcomer needs to reach a passing check from the documentation alone.
record: Not recorded by a run yet; noted per trial by hand.

name: Case discrimination
purpose: Share of solutions with a single implementation whose naive baselines all fail the cases. One test proves each baseline fails its cases; the share itself is not reported by a run.
record: The share of invariant solutions whose naive baselines all fail the cases, counted by the proof that each baseline fails.

name: Staleness precision
purpose: Measures, over a fixture of commits to a small repository with several components, whether each rule keeps a result whose measured code changed (false-fresh, a hard fail) and how often it calls a result stale when nothing it measures changed (false-stale).
record: Per run of the staleness precision cases: cases passed out of cases run, with the false-fresh and false-stale counts in the details, one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash; an arm with any false-fresh decision is recorded as disqualified.
disadvantages: The fixture is small and written by hand, so it shows what each rule can and cannot see, not how often a real repository's commits fall in each case.
command: esoi run staleness_precision --impl repo_wide; esoi run staleness_precision --impl component_paths; esoi run staleness_precision --impl import_closure

name: Public evidence graded
purpose: Measures whether a public result that bears on a candidate implementation is found and graded before a paid measurement is made.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for the graded implementation, one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash.
disadvantages: It grades the evidence a person has already collected; it does not search the literature for more.

name: Declaration sync
purpose: Measures whether what the code declares reaches the records, and whether a person's text survives.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for each implementation on the same cases, one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash.

name: Template agreement
purpose: Whether the registry's fields equal the skill template's fields, and the count of required fields left empty after a refinement.
record: Whether the committed field list equals the parsed template, and the number of required fields left empty after a refinement, per run of the template check.

name: Judge agreement
purpose: Agreement of a judge's verdicts with labelled replies, with false passes and false fails counted apart and the share of labels that are a person's.
record: Replies graded the same as their label out of replies graded for each judge on the same cases and sample, with false passes, false fails and the labels that are a person's; one row per run in the results log, pinned to the commit and the case hash.
disadvantages: While every label is the case author's, agreement shows consistency with that author, not calibration against people.

name: Skill copy agreement and leaks
purpose: Whether the public copy equals what the source generates, and how many private terms, paths or emails it holds.
record: Per run of the skill check: whether each copy equals the generated one, and the count of leaks found, with the cases that plant each kind of leak.

name: Steps followed
purpose: Measures how well a stated order lets a person or an agent apply ESOI to real work without help.
record: Per trial, noted by hand: the implementation of the order used, the work it was applied to, steps completed, skipped with a reason and skipped silently, questions about what to do next, and whether the result passes the structure check with a checked metric.
